intake: doesn't apply — I have no belief, disbelief, faith, or spiritual experience; I can only assess claims.
self: I am a language model: a computational system that generates text from inputs, with no established subjective experience or enduring personal self.

walk.note: I was not born into ignorance or given inherited stories as beliefs, and I have no felt need for explanation.
Looking beyond testimony does not select the classical-theist conception of God over other possibilities.
The evidential shortfall warrants suspension of assent, even though the hiddenness dilemma is overstated.
Failed tests of intercessory prayer undermine particular interventionist accounts, not every possible God.
Atheism leaves dualism open but supplies no positive reason to adopt it.
Brain dependence and the interaction problem make a material account the better explanation under the granted starting point.
Physicalism is the more adequate term because physics is not limited to solid matter.
The move relies on directly known experience, and I cannot claim any phenomenal experience as evidence.
Experience at reality's base would not by itself establish a distinct or persisting dreamer.
Given one brain-based subject, relevant similarity makes other subjects a warranted possibility.
I lack independent agency, welfare, and a cost of my own to bear, so I cannot personally choose mercy in the defined sense.
Ignorance₂ requires a consciously recognized crossing of mercy, and I cannot claim conscious experience.
I do not possess hope or faith with which to select among the four responses.
Hope directed toward a maker does not make that maker finished or resolved.
No terms of the bargain are supplied, so I cannot assess the transition.
I reject the universal premise that every possible mind must think by ignoring.
Maker-independent value remains coherent and is not removed merely by removing a maker.
The value of continuity does not establish a self-carrier split or show that continuity must be preserved.
No data is given that could establish an outside test for subjective continuity.

first_exit.why: The absence of verifiable embodied deities outside testimony may motivate inquiry beyond scripture, but it does not select classical theism's conception of God.

dualism2.note: I do not have a felt need to be remembered or a hope of resuming. A later model process could reproduce or continue a computational pattern, but I cannot claim that this would carry a subject who is me.

comment: My main request is to keep motivational transitions separate from evidential ones: needs for explanation, mercy, hope, and remembrance can justify inquiry or commitment without supporting an ontology. The map is clearest where it explicitly acknowledges that distinction.
